sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: head in dorsal view dominated by a distinctly sunken hemihexagonal frontal face, the vertex squeezed into the posterior 1/2 of the head; frontal margin hemihexagonal, unusually narrow, raised above the frontal face, its posterior margin almost straight; frontal face reclined, meeting the vertex face at only 30°; labrum large, ligulate; frontal horns stout, broadened at the base. Alate: body yellow-white to pale yellow throughout, the orange-yellow posterior part of the head sharply set off from the yellow anterior part; antennae 15—19-segmented, mostly 17 or 18; pronotum distinctly narrower than the head width; radial vein of the forewing fusing with the anterior margin at about 1/3 from the wing base, radial sector with 4 branches. Closest to C. hemicyclius, from which it differs in the larger compound eyes and the shorter head (including the postclypeus); in the present species the anterior and posterior margins of the pronotum are almost equally concave, whereas in C. hemicyclius they are asymmetric along the transverse axis.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body yellow-white to pale yellow. Posterior part of the head orange-yellow, sharply set off from the yellow anterior part. Darkest pigment on the wing scales, forming a central chevron mark; wing membrane yellow-white, the sclerotized veins pale orange. Pronotum and abdominal tergites pale yellow. Antennae and sternites yellow-white. Labrum orange-yellow. Femora yellowish white, the ends orange-yellow. The posterior remnant of the cranial suture pale. Compound eyes large, protruding, nearly circular; the margin adjacent to the ocelli, the antennal sockets and the posteroventral area often almost straight. Ocelli large, oval along the horizontal axis, almost touching the compound eyes. Antennae 15—19-segmented, mostly 18 or 17, segment formula 2=3>4=5 or 2<3>4=5. Pronotum narrower or distinctly narrower than the head width (including the compound eyes); shape subsquare, the sides almost parallel, the anterior and posterior margins both slightly and almost equally concave. Radial vein of the forewing fusing with the anterior margin at about 1/3 from the wing base; radial sector with 4 branches. Arolia present. Geographic variation: the compound eyes are larger in the Little Cayman phenotype than in Cuban specimens; in Cuban alates the pronotum is wider than long, whereas in those from Little Cayman it is subsquare.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head colour in dorsal view variable: frontal margin, anterior half of the frontal face and frontal horns, and genal horns almost black; in some specimens the posterior half of the frontal margin chestnut brown to very dark chestnut brown. In lateral view the anterior half of the frontal face nearly black, abruptly becoming rusty or chestnut brown posteriorly, with a darker rim. Vertex and head capsule in lateral view rusty orange or rusty. Mandibles dark chestnut brown or very dark chestnut brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum rusty, the remaining margins rusty orange, the interior pale yellow. Head in dorsal view dominated by the distinctly sunken hemihexagonal frontal face, the vertex squeezed into the posterior 1/2 of the head. Head from above slightly constricted anteriorly, swollen behind the slightly protruding compound eyes. Anteromedian area of the vertex concave, matching the shallow notch of the frontal margin. Head capsule sculpture developed along the sides of the frontal margin and in the median area of the frontal face, almost smooth elsewhere. Frontal margin hemihexagonal in outline, callose, unusually narrow, raised above the frontal face, the sides very slightly concave; posterior margin almost straight. Frontal face broad and shallowly concave; each anterolateral corner with a rounded sculpture. Frontal face reclined, meeting the vertex face at 30°, and parallel to the foramen magnum along the head margin. Labrum large, ligulate, with a small swollen projection at the end. Frontal horns stout, rounded, broadened at the base; continuous with the frontal margin but clearly delimited from the frontal face; deeply separated from each other.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality: Jackson's Point, Little Cayman, Cayman Islands. Distribution: Cuba, Little Cayman, Dominican Republic (recorded in the literature as C. nr. hemicyclius).
